Definition: perhaps from G3700 (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); the eye-"brow" or forehead, i.e. (figuratively) the brink of a precipice:--brow.
BiblicalUsage: The brow of the hill appears once, in Nazareth, when the people rose up and thrust Jesus out of the city and led Him to the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, intending to cast Him down headlong.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the brow of that hill shows how close anger sits to murder: the town that heard Jesus could not bear Him, and He passed through their midst and went His way.
